title: Shed Floor Bonfire Picnic Pot
tagline: Damp wrappers, one wellie and a doormat. Pudding is a lawnmower bag.

ingredients.item: soggy sparkler wrappers, wrung out like a sulky sponge
bristly doormat, chopped into bite-defying squares
garden twine, knotted beyond all hope
leaf mush from behind the shed
rake, for stirring and looking busy

steps:
Drag the cauldron to the shed, then yell, 'Hurrah!'
Plop in the wrappers, all limp, soggy and raw.

Squelch in the wellie, so muddy and wide,
With the smelly old sock tucked up snug inside.

Slap down the doormat in squares, flat and rough,
Then tangle the twine in a knotty great fluff.

Sprinkle the flowerpot crumbs, red and grim,
Then tip in the leaf mush until it's brimmed to the brim.

Stir with the rake till it slurps and goes glug,
Then spread out a blanket and give it a hug.
rhyme:
Wobble, wobble, shed-floor stew,
Soggy wrappers, plop in two!
Splat goes a wellie, mud-brown and wide,
With a smelly old sock still stuck inside.
Slap in the doormat, bristly and flat,
Then a twine-tangle lump, like a knotted-up hat.
Sprinkle the pot crumbs, gritty and red,
Add leaf-mush slime from the old garden bed.
Stir with a rake till it gloops and goes glug,
Picnic's ready. Come on, give it a hug!
image_prompt: A tartan picnic blanket holding a large black cauldron of grey-brown sludge. A muddy green wellington boot pokes out, with a stripy odd sock hanging from it. Around it sit damp doormat squares, a knotted ball of twine, red flowerpot crumbs, and limp, soggy cardboard sparkler wrappers draped over the rim.
alt_text: A black cauldron of grey sludge on a picnic blanket, with a muddy wellie, odd sock, doormat squares, twine and soggy cardboard wrappers.
caption_hook: Bonfire Night picnic, courtesy of the back of the shed. The wellie is the centrepiece, naturally. Which of these would you bring to the party?
